ledger.note: 1 July 1896: the Federated Malay States begin. 'These four states were brought together under the Treaty of Federation 1895' (Selangor, Perak, Negeri Sembilan and Pahang, 'four integrated protectorates'); the treaty took effect on 1 July 1896, and 'From 1896 to 1936, real power lay in the hands of the Resident-General' (Swettenham from 1 January 1896). Each state kept its hereditary ruler.

1 July 1896: Negeri Sembilan joins. It is the fourth of the 'four integrated protectorates' under the Treaty of Federation 1895; its own dossier ends in 1895 with the confederation joining the federation.

certainty.note: The four states' boundaries were fixed by the treaties with their rulers and the Residencies; the page names the four states and gives no boundary, so the outline is the modern states' (sharp); the Dindings and the Thai-ceded northern states are not part of it.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch. A colony Cliopatria lacks (inside the British Colonial Empire row). Two pages opened. Unsettled: (1) the start: the page says 'Federated: 1895' (Treaty of Federation) and gives 1 July 1896 as the day it took effect; 1896 is used (Negeri Sembilan's dossier ends in 1895, so no year is drawn twice; a renderer wanting the treaty year can use 1895). (2) The page gives no area or boundary: the outline is the four modern states plus Kuala Lumpur. (3) The 1909 Federal Council ('a further agreement between the British and Malay rulers was signed to establish the Federal Council'), the Chief Secretary office (1911) and the 1936 reduction of the Federal Secretaries to co-ordinating officers are constitutional, not territorial, and are not events. (4) Japan's Thai-bound cession of Kedah, Perlis, Kelantan and Terengganu (1943) and the Sumatra-Malaya administration are not on the page. (5) The Malayan Union is a successor that needs a dossier (se-04); the Unfederated Malay States are a counterpart that needs one too. (6) British Colonial Empire (eu-11) should carry a loss of these cells in 1896 and the occupation mirror; the four states' own dossiers end at 1876 (Perak, Selangor), 1888 (Pahang) and 1895 (Negeri Sembilan), so 1876-1895 the three Residencies are drawn as British Colonial Empire land.
